question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

As a boy, Charles was a __boor__ who bullied other kids in his neighbourhood.
solution:
The correct answer is "**gentleman**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An antonym is a word that means the opposite of another word.
 
• Now, let us understand the meaning of the given and the marked words:
 
 
• **"Boor" means a rude, uncultured person.**(बेअदब अदमी)
 
 
• Example: I can't invite a boor like him to dinner!
 
 
 
• **"Gentleman" means a polite, well-mannered man, which is the opposite of a boor.**(सज्जन) 
 
 
• Example: He acted like a gentleman during that fight.
 
 
 
 

Hence, **the correct answer is option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1, "creep", means a person who is unpleasant or creepy, but it doesn't necessarily imply rudeness or bullying behavior.(अप्रिय)
 
• Option 2, "blighter", is a British slang term that can mean a contemptible person. (हानि करनेवाला)
 
• Option 4, "scum", is a strong insult that implies extreme contempt, but it's not an antonym of "boor" because it doesn't have the connotation of rudeness.(मैल)
